_what: The recorded identity of the deployed artifact. Scripts read the namespace and the module names from here rather than restating them, so a gate cannot compare a constant with itself.

slots._module_hash_note: MEASURED on chain, from both nodes, never computed locally. A Pact 5 module hash covers its dependencies' hashes; slots depends on coin, and the test suite loads a vendored coin snapshot while mainnet runs a different coin — so a hash computed here will NEVER equal this one and proves nothing. VERIFY.md compares the CODE instead.
slots._annotated_source_note: pact/modules/slots.pact is, byte for byte, the code the deploy transaction carried; deploy-bytes/slots.pact is its (module …) region, which is what describe-module returns.

drand._module_hash_note: For THIS module a hash comparison is valid and is worth running: drand has no dependencies, holds no table and uses no other module, so the hash the REPL computes from pact/modules/drand.pact equals the one mainnet reports. It is also the literal slots pins in its `use`.
drand.governance: (enforce false) — sealed at deploy; it can never be upgraded
drand.deployed_for: roulette, on 2026-09-22; slots uses the same deployed module and deployed no verifier of its own

crank._note: The helper tarball the house's two helpers run, packed from the private repository at the commit the module was tagged from, reproducibly. Not published; deployments/mainnet01-chain-2.md says how its files differ from crank/ here.

beacon._note: slots pins the verifier by hash in its `use`, so it cannot silently settle from different verifier code. pact/tests/slots-pin-must-fail.repl is the control that proves the pin bites.

_audit_note: Reviewed internally, including from cold contexts by reviewers with no implementation history and by offensive engagements that executed their attacks. That is NOT a paid third-party engagement, and we do not present it as one. No external firm has been paid to review this contract.
